stem: Angular momentum of a single particle moving with constant speed along circular path:
options: remains same in magnitude and direction
changes in magnitude but remains same in the direction
remains same in magnitude but changes in the direction
solution:
$|\vec{L}| = mVr$, which is constant for constant speed.

And direction will be upward (perpendicular to the plane) and remain constant.

stem: If the source of light used in a Young's double slit experiment is changed from red to violet:
options: consecutive fringe lines will come closer.
the central bright fringe will become a dark fringe.
the intensity of minima will increase.
solution:
$\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

$\lambda_R > \lambda_V \Rightarrow \beta_R = \dfrac{\lambda_R D}{d} > \beta_V = \dfrac{\lambda_V D}{d}$

Fringe pattern will shrink. Option (A) is correct.

If radius of the $^{27}_{13}\text{Al}$ nucleus is estimated to be $3.6$ fermi then the radius of $^{125}_{52}\text{Te}$ nucleus be nearly-
solution:
Radius of a nucleus $\propto$ (Mass Number)$^{1/3}$

$\dfrac{R_{Te}}{R_{Al}} = \left(\dfrac{125}{27}\right)^{1/3} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$\Rightarrow R_{Te} = R_{Al}\times\dfrac{5}{3} = 6$ fermi

Which one of the following compounds would have the highest heat of hydrogenation?
solution: The heat of hydrogenation of an alkene depends upon its stability. Higher the stability, lower the heat of hydrogenation. Since $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ has no substituent, it is the least stable alkene and hence has the highest heat of hydrogenation.
subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation

Which of the following will respond to Cannizzaro's reaction?
solution:
(a) $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CHO}$, 2,2-dimethylpropanal (no $\alpha$-H)

(b) $\text{CH}_3-\text{CHO}$, acetaldehyde ($\alpha$-H present)

(c) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, propionaldehyde ($\alpha$-H present)

(d) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}=\text{CHCHO}$, cinnamaldehyde ($\alpha$-H present)

Only aldehydes without $\alpha$-H undergo Cannizzaro reaction.
